failures.title: Alfa Romeo 670050436 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Low‑Pressure Fuel Pump Failure - sudden stalling without warning
items.whatHappens: The low‑pressure fuel pump can fail without warning, cutting off fuel delivery immediately and leaving the car disabled. This issue has led to over 2,100 customer complaints, nearly 500 warranty claims, five crashes, and three injuries in the US. The recall covers 53,849 vehicles in the US and 3,300 in Canada. Affected models include 2017-2019 Giulias and 2018-2019 Stelvios equipped with the 2.9‑litre V6.
items.repairVsReplace: Fuel pump replacement is a standalone repair - but many owners report repeated pump replacements with no fix in sight, and the part has been on back order. A fix is still being developed as of late 2025.

items.title: Secondary Oil Pump Failure - cylinder shutdown codes
items.whatHappens: The secondary oil pump (auxiliary pump) can fail, with the shaft seizing and twisting. Symptoms include cylinder shutdown codes (typically cylinders 1, 2, and 3). The pump design was revised in June 2019. This affects early production QVs, with one reported failure at 35,000 miles.
items.repairVsReplace: Oil pump replacement is a standalone repair costing approximately $789-$982 (parts only). If the pump fails completely and oil starvation occurs, the engine may require full replacement.

items.title: Oil Consumption - valve stem seals and piston rings
items.whatHappens: Some 670050436 engines experience oil consumption, particularly on higher‑mileage units. This can be caused by valve stem seal degradation or piston ring sticking, especially on cars that have been tracked or driven hard. Symptoms include blue smoke on start‑up and needing to top up oil between services.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, valve stem seal replacement is a standalone repair (cylinder‑head‑off job). If piston rings are the cause, a full rebuild or replacement may be more cost‑effective.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 670050436
variants.intro: The 670050436 is the primary engine code for the Alfa Romeo 690T 2.9‑litre twin‑turbo V6, produced from 2015 to the present. It is a 90° V6 with a closed‑deck aluminium block, DOHC valvetrain, and both port and direct injection. The engine is Ferrari‑derived - essentially a cut‑down version of the 3.9‑litre F154 V8 used in the Ferrari 488 GTB. Where to find the engine code: - On the engine block - a stamped plate near the front of the V - On the V5C registration document - under engine number - Via an Alfa Romeo VIN decoder - the engine code is part of the vehicle identification Commonly confused codes: - 670052588 - a related engine code used in some Quadrifoglio models - 670052721 - another variant of the 690T engine - EED - the sales code for the 2.9L V6 engine in US market documentation - 2.0T GME - the 2.0‑litre turbo four‑cylinder used in non‑Quadrifoglio Giulia and Stelvio models; completely different engine

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 670050436 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used 670050436 is a viable option given the relatively low availability of reconditioned units. However, the engine's known weak points - fuel pump and oil pump - must be addressed. Only buy with documented evidence that the fuel pump recall has been completed and the oil pump is the revised (post‑06/2019) design. Used units typically cost £5,000-£6,500. Used engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A proper 670050436 recon addresses the engine's known weaknesses: new fuel pump (latest revision), revised oil pump (post‑2019 design), new valve stem seals, piston rings (if needed), and a full gasket set. This is the right call for owners who want a reliable, long‑lasting unit - the 690T is a masterpiece of engineering when properly refreshed. Expect £7,000-£9,000 with 12-24 months warranty. related.title: Engines Related to the Alfa Romeo 670050436

items.description: the 670050436 (690T) is Alfa Romeo's first modern twin‑turbo V6, introduced with the Giulia Quadrifoglio in 2015. There was no direct predecessor in the Alfa Romeo lineup; the previous V6s were the Busso V6 (1990s-2005) and the GM‑derived V6s (2005-2015), both naturally aspirated and completely unrelated.

the 690T remains in production as Alfa Romeo's flagship performance engine. However, Alfa Romeo has announced that the V6 will be phased out in some markets as the brand transitions to electrification. The 2025 Giulia Quadrifoglio may be the last V6‑powered Alfa Romeo.

items.question: What are the common problems with the 670050436 engine?
items.answer: The most documented failures are low‑pressure fuel pump failure (sudden stalling, subject to a recall) and secondary oil pump failure (pre‑2019 vehicles, causing cylinder shutdown codes). The fuel pump recall affects 2017-2019 Giulias and 2018-2019 Stelvios. Oil pump design was revised in June 2019 - verify revision date on any used unit. Oil consumption can occur on higher‑mileage units with valve stem seal wear.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 670050436?
items.answer: A reconditioned 670050436 is the safer choice because it addresses the engine's known weak points (fuel pump, oil pump, valve stem seals) and comes with a warranty. Used units are cheaper but must have documented fuel pump recall completion and oil pump revision date. Given the complexity of this Ferrari‑derived engine, reconditioning is strongly recommended for reliability.
